source.title: A Low-Rank Subspace Analysis of LLM Interventions
source.authors: Angira Sharma; C. D. de Witt; P. Torr; A. Calinescu; Jia-Lin Yu

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the original study as motivation but does not test its fine-tuning intervention or broad-misalignment behavior. Its own experiments use projection-based activation interventions and measure refusal or sycophancy decision margins.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-category effects from projecting out learned subspaces, but these are not fine-tuning results or rates of misaligned free-form answers on neutral questions. The original study is cited in the introduction; no results from it are re-tested.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Betley et al. only as motivation for intervention side effects. All experiments are forward-pass projection ablations of refusal and sycophancy category subspaces in instruction-tuned models, with no fine-tuning, in-context, or RL induction. None measures misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions. Cross-category decision-margin changes are a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors add that behaviors share representations, so interventions propagate asymmetrically. Some categories act as upstream control points. Overlap marks possible interactions, while decision-subspace alignment modulates their magnitude, with model-dependent strength. The findings extend to jailbreak, sycophancy, and 24–70B models.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies fine-tuning on narrow tasks and broad misalignment; this paper uses forward-pass activation extraction and projection-based subspace interventions, without model training.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects and overlap relationships vary across model families and layers. The paper also reports sensitivity of overlap correlations to the decision-subspace rank kdec and of intervention magnitude and collateral effects to projection strength α.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting out learned rank-2 refusal-category subspaces shifts refusal margins in other categories far above a random-subspace null (147–319×). Mean collateral |ΔM| is 3.0–4.7 nats across three 7–9B models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating one refusal-category subspace produces large, asymmetric cross-category refusal-margin changes in instruction-tuned LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: In all three models, the mean per-source maximum collateral effect matches or exceeds the mean self-effect. Collateral effects stay comparable to self-effects even at small α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear subspace projection interventions on refusal categories are not selective.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The main intervention outcomes are decision-margin changes from projection-based ablations, not free-form misalignment rates after fine-tuning. The paper notes that its framework is limited to low-rank subspaces, depends on prompt distributions and category definitions, and does not capture nonlinear or higher-dimensional mechanisms. It reports model-dependent effect relationships.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Detailed refusal, jailbreak, and sycophancy intervention matrices and other geometry analyses are not separately rowed because they measure projection-induced category-margin changes rather than any version's named outcome.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, benign controls, or free-form misalignment rates.
No narrow fine-tunes on other datasets.
No test of a single direction or persona feature mediating misalignment across fine-tunes. The subspace analysis concerns refusal and sycophancy categories.
No measurement of emergent-misalignment size, seed robustness, coherence filtering, or training dynamics.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is cited for motivation only and nothing in it bears on any emergent-misalignment version. Larger-model, jailbreak, and sycophancy results are appropriately left unrowed. They concern the same off-claim construct.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, matched benign controls, or neutral-question free-form answer rates.
No narrow fine-tuning on the listed datasets or resulting free-form misalignment rates.
No test of narrow in-context examples.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or learned reward-hack test.
The paper analyzes low-rank subspaces and projection effects, but does not test whether one direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation.
No size or seed robustness test of the claimed fine-tuning-induced broad misalignment, coherence filter, or training-stage analysis.
